distinguishing_features: Proposes active modulation of flow geometry via VFD speed and feed rate control, not just inference
Uses flow and pressure telemetry to predict and prevent belt rip before clump arrival, not detect ongoing misalignment
Implements pulsed velocity isolation to create a 'vacuum zone' at transfer point
Targets kinetic energy reduction of tramp metal clumps via dynamic system response
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Preventing conveyor belt edge rip caused by high-inertia impact of tramp metal clumps at transfer points without adding hardware or relying solely on detection
parsed.viable_reason: The mechanism assumes precise clump isolation and stress reduction via flow modulation without demonstrating feasibility of timing or control accuracy required at 4 m/s belt speed.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The approach extends inference-based control (as in prior art 3) to active intervention, but the specific method of pulsed velocity isolation is not sufficiently distinct from routine application of existing control logic to flow and speed variables.
